findings: Misleading commit message on RTL arrows — The commit claims 'Fix 1: Reverse navigation arrows in Quran reader for RTL flow' but no functional change was made. DirectionalIcon already handles RTL correctly; only comments were updated. Either document this as 'verified correct, no change needed' or remove the claim from the commit message.

Blur fix addresses non-existent issue — Fix #2 claims to verify 'no excessive blur in Quran index header' but the quran_index_page.dart header never had BackdropFilter. The surah_reader_page.dart modals use sigma 8, which is reasonable. Without the original bug screenshots, this appears to be a phantom fix. Clarify what blur issue was actually observed.

Layout fixes are mostly reformatting — Fix #4 claims to 'verify consistent spacing and alignment across dashboard sections' but the diff shows only code style changes (multi-line formatting, import cleanup). No padding, margin, or spacing values were adjusted in the dashboard body. Document what layout issues were identified and fixed, or acknowledge this was a code cleanup pass.

Scope creep with unrelated changes — The commit includes removal of the azkar section, addition of RamadanCountdownCard, refactoring of accountability logic, and new prayer key tracking. These are legitimate changes but unrelated to the four stated UI fixes. They make the diff harder to review and conflate feature work with bug fixes.

Missing verification of glassmorphic readability — The new header uses BackdropFilter with sigma 10 and semi-transparent overlays (white 18%, gold 8%). The review cannot verify whether text remains readable in both light and dark modes, especially for users with visual impairments. The plan called for testing on physical devices and checking performance (no jank), but no verification note was provided.
